title: Danny Boyle Talks Returning to Telluride and Fighting to Make His Tabloid Sensation ‘Ink’
summary: The Oscar winner also explains his decision to use AI tools in 30 seconds of the film: "I didn't want an imitation Thatcher."

title: ‘The Illusion of an Everlasting Summer’ Review: A Photographer’s Portrait of Two Argentine Cousins Poignantly Captures the Passage of Time
summary: Telluride: Alessandra Sanguinetti chronicles the shared and separate lives of Guillermina and Belinda from childhood into their mid-thirties.

title: ‘Making Marie Antoinette’ Review: Eleanor Coppola’s Tender Documentary About Her Daughter’s Masterpiece Doubles as a Wistful Self-Portrait
summary: Telluride: Two generations of women see each other through the years in this marvelous documentary cobbled together from 80 hours of "Marie Antoinette" set footage.

title: ‘Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger’ Review: The Gallaghers’ Concert Doc Is a Reason for Celebration
summary: While the setlist might be a bit long for more casual fans, this joyous chronicle of the Oasis reunion tour offers an inspiring tale of forgiveness and reconciliation.

title: Robert Pattinson Won’t Be the Only ‘Primetime’ Star to Generate Oscar Buzz
summary: Outside of Pattinson's big swing as "To Catch a Predator" host Chris Hansen, Lance Oppenheim's feature debut "Primetime" serves as a showcase for stars Merritt Wever and Skyler Gisondo as well.

title: ‘Elsinore’ and ‘The Liberation’ Launch TV Stars Andrew Scott and Carrie Coon Into the Oscar Race
summary: Telluride Day One boasted two world premieres with heart-rending performances.

title: ‘The Difficult Bride’ Turns South Asia’s Beloved Wedding Tropes Into Feminist Folk Horror at Venice
summary: Venice: One of the few female filmmakers to break out of Bangladesh, Rubaiyat Hossain’s fourth feature resists genre categorizations. But it makes a meal of a creepy urban myth the director heard as a seven-year-old girl involving a now-shuttered elite beauty salon in Dhaka.

title: What I Learned Watching Six Hours of Gen-AI Short Films for the Reply AI Film Festival
summary: IndieWire's Brian Welk reflects on his experience as a jury member for the upcoming AI film festival taking place in Venice.

title: ‘Primetime’ Review: Robert Pattinson Is Even Creepier Than IRL Chris Hansen in a Bleakly Invigorating ‘To Catch a Predator’ Thriller
summary: Venice: Lance Oppenheim scuzzies up his fiction feature debut about hidden-camera, reality-TV exploitation with a grim style and often twisted performances from Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo, and singer/songwriter Phoebe Bridgers.

title: ‘Citizen Osama’ Review: A Direct, Disarming View of Daily Horrors in Gaza from the POV of a Journalist and New Father
summary: Venice: Filmed in secret, Ahmed Hassouna’s discerning doc wears its heart unassumingly on its sleeve and holds its no-frills camera setup sturdily in its hands.

title: ‘The Row’ Review: A Man Rows Across the Atlantic in a Documentary that Makes His Inspirational Voyage Feel More Like a Vanity Project
summary: Telluride: Tez Steinberg’s two solo rowing expeditions are impressive, even if Bryan Fogel’s profile feels unexamined.

title: ‘Elsinore’ Review: Andrew Scott’s Towering Performance as a Dying Actor Can’t Overcome AIDS-Movie Awards Bait Clichés
summary: Telluride: Scott vividly portrays "Gandhi" and "Chariots of Fire" star Ian Charleson, who made "Hamlet" his final role at the National Theatre, but the movie around him sinks into forgettability.
